answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may endorse a task, then cap each stake’s influence and slash it when endorsements repeatedly prove fraudulent. A sybil operator can forge names cheaply, but cannot multiply credible influence without locking up more capital and risking loss; honest agents can bridge reputation across tasks only after verified outcomes, so new identities start with little weight. A pigment-like cosmetic signal earns no trust on its own.
